thread.title: U.S. Stocks Up Moderately But This Foreign GDP Shocks

author: PAUL WHITFIELD
title: U.S. Stocks Up Moderately But This Foreign GDP Shocks
text:
U.S. stock indexes advanced early Wednesday as GDP matched the consensus expectation. Meanwhile, India's GDP came in at 7.2%, giving it the title for the world's fastest growing major economy.
X The Nasdaq popped 0.4%, while the S&P 500 and the Dow Jones industrial average rose 0.3% and 0.4% respectively.
Volume in the stock market today was up slightly on the Nasdaq.
The second reading on fourth quarter GDP rolled in at 2.5%, matching the Street's consensus view. Recent GDP releases have sparked all-or-nothing reactions in the stock market. In the past 10 GDP releases not including Wednesday's report, the Nasdaq either rose or fell by more than 1% five times and rose or fell by 0.1% or less five times.
India also reported its Q4 GDP this morning. The 7.2% spurt was higher than the 6.9% gain that analysts expected. India's growth surpassed China's 6.8% Q4 gain to grab the lead position among major economies.
Barclays iPath India ( INP ) benchmark exchange traded fund is down 3% year to date after rising 41% last year.
Among the India stocks trading on U.S. exchanges, three have Composite Ratings of 91 or better. The Composite Rating combines all five IBD ratings into a single number. A rating of 91 means the stock is in the top 9%.
The three highly rated India stocks are HDFC Bank ( HDB ), which carries a 91 Composite Rating; tech services provider Infosys ( INFY ), which is rated 94; and outsourcer WNS Holdings ( WNS ), which is rated a best possible 99.
WNS has shaped a base-on-base pattern with a 46.10 buy point.
In the 30-component Dow Jones industrial average, Apple ( AAPL ) advanced 0.7%, staying just under a recent high. Boeing ( BA ) rose 1.8%, marking a new high.
Among IBD's 197 industry groups , Retail-Apparel/Shoes scored strong gain. TJX Companies ( TJX ) gapped up 7% to a new high. Urban Outfitters ( URBN ) and American Eagle Outfitters ( AEO ) notched solid gains but remain in their 5% buy zone.
Economic News Chicago's purchasing managers index for February came in at 61.9, below the consensus figure of 65 and under the lowest estimate (62) in the range. The Chicago gauge measures both manufacturing and nonmanufacturing firms.
The National Association of Realtors' pending home sales for January dived 4.7%, badly missing the consensus estimate for a 0.3% gain.
